overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts performance reveals a clear viewer preference for extreme astronomical phenomena and hypothetical 'What If' space scenarios. Videos exploring bizarre planetary environments (e.g., liquid diamond planets, dark planets, extreme rainfall worlds) generated the highest views and engagement (likes-per-view up to 0.037). Conversely, standard biological facts and psychological tricks underperformed in recent cohorts. The audience responds best to high-concept cosmic wonder paired with immersive 'What If' immersion hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved over 970 to 1,028 views rapidly with high like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical planetary descent scenarios involving extreme physics, exotic materials, or lethal environments.

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Cosmic Realities & Extreme Weather on Exoplanets
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring unusual planetary traits (e.g., 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b', 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') drove strong engagement exceeding 700-1,000 views.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form spotlights on verified exoplanets with extreme, counter-intuitive physical properties.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content focusing on brain functions, fake memories, or songs stuck in your head (e.g., mGEgENcGcNE, 5AN7LUgqarc) consistently stalled under 60 views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone human psychology shorts unless tied directly to extreme survival or space-induced physiological changes.

weak_patterns.pattern: Standard Animal Trivia without Narrative Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (AXAfwrzzEdU) saw mediocre traction compared to cosmic content.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content exclusively toward cinematic animal survival or prehistoric evolutionary mysteries rather than simple listicle facts.
